c_module_level_file_or_network_io_at_imp.detail: grep + manual inspection of every top-level (column-0) statement in all 13 vendored files found no open()/read_text()/read_bytes()/json.load()/requests./urllib request call/Path.glob()/os.listdir() executed outside a def/class body. Every file that performs I/O gates it behind a function, and every file with a __main__ block (truth_classify.py, judge.py, items.py, harvest_variants.py, time_rule.py, verify_hooks.py, unit_checks.py, hf_probe.py, panel.py) guards it with `if __name__ == "__main__":`.

c_module_level_file_or_network_io_at_imp.finding: related-but-distinct: sys.path mutation at import time
c_module_level_file_or_network_io_at_imp.detail: 8 of the 13 files execute sys.path.insert(...) at module level (see list below). This is not itself a file read or network call, but it is an import-time SIDE EFFECT that mutates the process-global sys.path, which is what lets the module-level 'from common import ...' lines resolve at all; once these files live under vendor/ as a package this mutation is redundant (vendor/ is already on the same sys.path entry as the importing package) but still fires and can shadow unrelated modules named 'common' elsewhere on sys.path for the rest of the process.

patches_applied.why: The vendored copies resolved the workspace as Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1], which is correct where they were written (H1/src/X.py -> H1) but WRONG once copied to src/vendor/X.py (-> src/). Symptoms observed: empty src/{assets,harvest,logs,private,results} directories created by import-time mkdir, and a FileNotFoundError when ams_reimpl looked for src/assets/ams_spec.json. The vendored common.CHAIN is additionally ISOLATED to logs/vendor_h1_chain.jsonl because H1's chain record format is incompatible with this artifact's logs/chain.jsonl. No numerical code is touched; only path constants.
